sources.title: FDA — Medical Product Communications That Are Consistent With the FDA-Required Labeling (Guidance)
FDA — Brief Summary and adequate directions / fair balance expectations for Rx advertising (overview pages)

medical.title: Consistent with FDA-required labeling
medical.check_prompt: Using supplied US PI / labeling, flag product claims that are inconsistent with labeled indication, limitations, or safety. If PI not supplied, [GAP] — do not recall a label from memory.

medical.title: Fair balance of risk information
medical.check_prompt: For HCP promotional content, check whether risk information is presented with prominence reasonably comparable to benefits (fair balance). Flag benefit-heavy layouts that bury risks.

medical.title: Clinical superiority without adequate evidence
medical.check_prompt: Flag superiority or 'best' language without a supplied adequate and well-controlled comparative basis in materials.

legal.title: False or misleading impression
legal.check_prompt: Flag omissions or juxtapositions that would make a true statement misleading to an HCP reader. Note as legal concern for counsel — do not declare violation.

legal.title: Reminder vs product claim ad
legal.check_prompt: If materials look like reminder advertising, check they do not include representations/suggestions about the product beyond reminder limits. Ambiguity → [GAP] for classification.

regulatory.title: Brief summary / ISI presence for product claim ads
regulatory.check_prompt: For product-claim HCP ads, check whether brief summary / important safety information is present or clearly linked as required for the format. Missing → finding; if format unknown, [GAP].

regulatory.title: Pre-approval / investigational promotion
regulatory.check_prompt: Flag promotion of an investigational or unapproved use as if approved. Investigational disclosures must be explicit if present in materials.

regulatory.title: Companion diagnostic or REMS silence
regulatory.check_prompt: If supplied PI mentions REMS or companion diagnostic requirements, flag promotional copy that omits them when discussing use.
